steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our text-to-3D paper, where we fine-tune a text-to-image diffusion model to generate multi-view 2.5D (depth/normal) images and then fuse them into a textured mesh. Explain the weaknesses of SDS-based and direct 3D generation, why 2.5D is a good middle ground, how our pipeline works, and list the contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. 3D generation is hot; SDS-based methods (DreamFusion) and their problems
2. Direct 3D generation from 3D data and the data-scale problem
3. Our approach: multi-view 2.5D diffusion
4. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Text-to-3D via SDS
- 3D content from generative models: heated topic in the past year
- applications: game and film industries, autonomous driving simulation, virtual reality
- DreamFusion: optimize NeRF using pre-trained 2D text-to-image diffusion + score distillation sampling (SDS); text-to-3D of arbitrary objects, no 3D data
- indirect 3D distribution modeling -> worse quality
- DreamFusion + follow-ups: low success rate, multi-face Janus problem

2. Direct 3D generation
- train on large-scale 3D data
- diffusion for point clouds; denoise diffusion on signed distance field (SDF)
- specific 3D representation + specific 3D dataset (e.g. ShapeNet); good results on objects similar to training set
- 3D datasets too small vs. text-image data
- even with largest 3D dataset: hard to train 3D diffusion for diverse text-to-3D

3. Our approach
- extend text-to-2D models to denoising diffusion on multi-view 2.5D depth/normal data
- vs. full 3D (point clouds, meshes): 1) 2.5D easier to capture/collect (depth from active sensors); 2) depth/normal maps align with images -> adapt/fine-tune from pre-trained 2D RGB model
- full 3D needs 2.5D maps from multiple views -> generate multi-view images with content consistency
- fine-tune text-to-image diffusion on multi-view 2.5D renderings from Objaverse
- adapted to 2.5D; joint multi-view distribution via injecting multi-view info into self-attention layers
- inference: multi-view images generated synchronously with schedulers like DDIM; fused into mesh by differentiable rasterization
- seconds vs. ~30 minutes for SDS-based methods
- evaluated with complex prompts vs. SDS-based + direct 3D methods: complex geometry, diversity, high fidelity

4. Contributions
- multi-view 2.5D diffusion: explicit 3D geometry distribution + generalization of large-scale pre-trained 2D diffusion
- efficient differentiable rasterization: textured mesh from multi-view normal maps + RGB images
- pipeline: diverse, mode-seeking-free, high-fidelity 3D generation in only 10 seconds

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Creating 3D content with generative models has been a heated research topic in the past year, and it is key to many downstream applications, including the game and film industries, autonomous driving simulation, and virtual reality. In particular, DreamFusion was proposed, which optimizes a neural radiance field (NeRF) using a pre-trained 2D text-to-image diffusion model and the score distillation sampling (SDS) technique. It showed promising results for text-to-3D generation of arbitrary objects without using any 3D data. However, because the 3D probability distribution is modeled indirectly, the final generation quality inevitably gets worse. For example, DreamFusion and its follow-ups report that the overall success rate of generation is low and that there is the multi-face Janus problem.

Another line of work does direct 3D generation by training on large-scale 3D data. For example, some works apply the probabilistic diffusion model to generate point clouds and others model the denoise diffusion process on signed distance field (SDF). These methods usually use a specific 3D representation and train the denoise diffusion on it with a specific 3D dataset, e.g., ShapeNet, and they show high-quality results on objects that are similar to the training set. But the current 3D datasets are still too small compared with the text-image data. Even with the largest 3D dataset that is available, it is still hard to train a 3D diffusion model for diverse text-to-3D generation.

- our approach: extend text-to-2D models to denoising diffusion on multi-view 2.5D depth/normal data
- why 2.5D over point clouds/meshes: 1) easier to capture/collect (depth from active sensors); 2) aligns with images -> fine-tune from pre-trained 2D RGB model
- full 3D needs multi-view 2.5D maps -> model must generate content-consistent multi-view images
- fine-tune on multi-view 2.5D renderings from Objaverse; adapt to 2.5D; joint multi-view distribution by injecting multi-view info into self-attention layers
- inference: synchronous multi-view generation with DDIM-like schedulers, fused into mesh by differentiable rasterization
- seconds vs. 30 minutes for SDS-based methods
- evaluation with complex prompts vs. SDS-based and direct 3D methods: complex geometry, diversity, high fidelity
- contributions: multi-view 2.5D diffusion model; differentiable rasterization from normal maps + RGB; pipeline, diverse, mode-seeking-free, high-fidelity in 10 seconds

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Creating 3D content with generative models has been a heated research topic in the past year, and it is key to many downstream applications, including the game and film industries, autonomous driving simulation, and virtual reality. In particular, DreamFusion was proposed, which optimizes a neural radiance field (NeRF) using a pre-trained 2D text-to-image diffusion model and the score distillation sampling (SDS) technique. It showed promising results for text-to-3D generation of arbitrary objects without using any 3D data. However, because the 3D probability distribution is modeled indirectly, the final generation quality inevitably gets worse. For example, DreamFusion and its follow-ups report that the overall success rate of generation is low and that there is the multi-face Janus problem.

Another line of work does direct 3D generation by training on large-scale 3D data. For example, some works apply the probabilistic diffusion model to generate point clouds and others model the denoise diffusion process on signed distance field (SDF). These methods usually use a specific 3D representation and train the denoise diffusion on it with a specific 3D dataset, e.g., ShapeNet, and they show high-quality results on objects that are similar to the training set. But the current 3D datasets are still too small compared with the text-image data. Even with the largest 3D dataset that is available, it is still hard to train a 3D diffusion model for diverse text-to-3D generation.

In this work we instead extend existing text-to-2D models to a denoising diffusion process on multi-view 2.5D depth/normal data. Compared with full 3D representations like 3D point clouds or meshes, 1) 2.5D information like depth or normal is much easier to capture or collect (e.g., depth from active sensors); 2) the depth and normal maps align perfectly with the image data, so it is possible to adapt and fine-tune a 2.5D model from a pre-trained 2D RGB model. To construct full 3D models we need 2.5D maps seen from multiple perspectives. So the target diffusion model has to be able to generate multi-view images that are consistent in content. In practice we fine-tune existing text-to-image diffusion models on multi-view 2.5D renderings from the Objaverse dataset. This adapts the models to 2.5D information, and it also captures the joint multi-view distribution through a structural modification that injects multi-view information into the self-attention layers. At inference, the multi-view images are generated synchronously with common schedulers like DDIM, and then they are fused directly into a mesh by differentiable rasterization. The whole generation process takes seconds, which is much faster than SDS-based methods that usually take 30 minutes. We evaluate the system extensively with complex text prompts and compare it with both SDS-based and direct 3D generation methods, and it shows it can generate 3D textured meshes with complex geometry, diversity, and high fidelity.

The major contributions of the paper are:

- We propose to approach 3D generation by training a multi-view 2.5D diffusion model, which models the 3D geometry distribution explicitly and also inherits the strong generalization ability of large-scale pre-trained 2D image diffusion.

- We introduce an efficient differentiable rasterization scheme that optimizes a textured mesh directly from the multi-view normal maps and RGB images.

- We design a generation pipeline that gets diverse, mode-seeking-free, and high-fidelity 3D content generation in only 10 seconds.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Creating 3D content from generative models has become a heated research topic in the past year, and it is key to a variety of downstream applications, including the game and film industries, autonomous driving simulation, and virtual reality. Specifically, DreamFusion [1] was proposed to optimize a neural radiance field (NeRF) [2] using a pre-trained 2D text-to-image diffusion model and the score distillation sampling (SDS) technique, showing promising results for text-to-3D generation of arbitrary objects without any 3D data. However, the indirect modeling of the 3D probability distribution inevitably deteriorates the final generation quality. For example, DreamFusion and its follow-ups [3,4,5,6] report that the overall generation success rate is low and that the multi-face Janus problem exists.

Another line of work focuses on direct 3D generation by training on large-scale 3D data. For example, [7,8] apply the probabilistic diffusion model for point cloud generation and [9,10] model the denoise diffusion process on signed distance field (SDF). These methods usually adopt a specific 3D representation and train the denoise diffusion on it using a specific 3D dataset, e.g., ShapeNet [11], showing high-quality results on objects similar to the training set. However, the scale of current 3D datasets is still too small compared with text-image data [12]. Even with the largest available 3D dataset [13], it remains challenging to train a 3D diffusion model for diverse text-to-3D generation.

In this work, we instead extend existing text-to-2D models to a denoising diffusion process on multi-view 2.5D depth/normal data. Compared with full 3D representations such as 3D point clouds or meshes, 1) 2.5D information such as depth or normal is much easier to capture or collect (e.g., depth provided by active sensors); 2) depth and normal maps align perfectly with image data, making it possible to adapt and fine-tune a 2.5D model from a pre-trained 2D RGB model. To construct full 3D models, 2.5D maps viewed from multiple perspectives are necessary, so the target diffusion model must be capable of generating multi-view images with content consistency. In practice, we fine-tune existing text-to-image diffusion models on multi-view 2.5D renderings from the Objaverse dataset [13]. On the one hand, the models are adapted to 2.5D information; on the other hand, the joint multi-view distribution is captured through a structural modification that injects multi-view information into the self-attention layers. During inference, multi-view images are generated synchronously by common schedulers like DDIM [14] and then fused directly into a mesh by differentiable rasterization. The whole generation process completes in seconds, significantly faster than SDS-based methods, which typically take 30 minutes. The system is extensively evaluated with complex text prompts and compared with both SDS-based and direct 3D generation methods, demonstrating its capability to generate 3D textured meshes with complex geometry, diversity, and high fidelity.

To summarize, the major contributions of the paper include:

- We propose to approach the 3D generation task by training a multi-view 2.5D diffusion model, which explicitly models the 3D geometry distribution while inheriting the strong generalization ability of large-scale pre-trained 2D image diffusion.

- We introduce an efficient differentiable rasterization scheme to optimize a textured mesh directly from multi-view normal maps and RGB images.

- We carefully design a generation pipeline that achieves diverse, mode-seeking-free, and high-fidelity 3D content generation in only 10 seconds.
